parts.title: Campus Conversation: Asking a Professor About a Late Paper
script: Listen to a conversation between a student and her professor.
Professor Miller, do you have a minute? I wanted to talk about my history paper.
Of course. Come in. Is there a problem?
Well, the paper is due tomorrow, but I got sick last week and could not finish the research. I only have half of it written.
I am sorry to hear that. Did you see a doctor?
Yes, I went to the campus health center. I have a note from them.
Good. Bring the note to me, and I can give you a three-day extension. The new deadline would be Monday.
Thank you so much. Should I send the paper by email or bring a printed copy?
Please upload it to the class website. I no longer accept printed papers.
Okay. One more thing. Could I visit your office hours on Friday to talk about my conclusion?
Certainly. I am in my office from two to four on Fridays. But come early, because many students visit that day.
I will be there at two. Thanks again, Professor.
Now get ready to answer the questions.
Listen again to part of the conversation.
Certainly. I am in my office from two to four on Fridays. But come early, because many students visit that day.
I will be there at two. Thanks again, Professor.

questions.q: Why does the student visit the professor?
o: To ask for more time to finish a paper
To ask about her grade on an exam
questions.exp: She is sick and needs an extension.

questions.q: What does the student need to give the professor to get the extension?
o: A printed copy of the paper
A note from the health center
questions.exp: The professor asks for the note from the health center.
The new deadline would be Monday.

questions.q: Why does the professor say, "come early, because many students visit that day"?
o: To warn the student that his office may be busy
To tell her the office closes at two
To say she should not come
To ask her to bring other students

questions.q: What will the student probably do next?
o: Visit office hours on Friday at two
questions.exp: She says she will be there at two.

parts.title: Academic Lecture: How Bees Communicate
script: Listen to part of a lecture in a biology class.
Today we will talk about how honeybees communicate. Bees cannot speak, but they can share information in a very interesting way. They dance.

Imagine a bee finds a field of flowers far from the hive. When she returns, she performs what scientists call the waggle dance. She moves in a figure-eight shape, and in the middle she shakes her body quickly.

This dance tells the other bees two things. First, the direction of the flowers. The angle of the dance compared with the sun shows the direction. Second, the distance. A longer waggle means the flowers are farther away.
Now, the bees inside the hive are in the dark, so how do they follow the dance? They touch the dancing bee with their antennae and feel her movements.
Scientists first described this dance in the 1940s. A researcher named Karl von Frisch watched thousands of bees and studied their movements. He won a Nobel Prize for this work in 1973.
Interestingly, if the flowers are very close, less than about fifty meters, the bee does a different dance, called the round dance. It does not show direction, because the flowers are easy to find.
So, to review: the waggle dance gives direction and distance, and the round dance says that food is nearby.
Now get ready to answer the questions.
Listen again to part of the lecture.
Now, the bees inside the hive are in the dark, so how do they follow the dance? They touch the dancing bee with their antennae and feel her movements.

questions.q: What is the lecture mainly about?
o: How bees share information by dancing
questions.exp: The lecture is about bee dances.

questions.q: What does a longer waggle in the dance show?
questions.exp: A longer waggle means a greater distance.

questions.q: How do bees in the dark hive follow the dance?
o: They listen to a loud sound
They touch the dancing bee with their antennae
questions.exp: They feel her movements with their antennae.

questions.q: Who first described the waggle dance?
Why does the professor say, "the bees inside the hive are in the dark"?
o: To explain why bees cannot see the dance and must feel it
To show that bees sleep at night
To explain why hives are warm
questions.exp: It leads to the explanation about touching.

questions.q: What does the round dance probably tell other bees?
o: The flowers are very near the hive
The flowers are in another country
questions.exp: Round dance means food is nearby.
